items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: We also had with us Joan Hill, who had been my common law step-daughter, if some law of that kind exists.

ctx.x: But the surprise of the night and it was an unexpected one, was that Billie Holliday was at Minton's this night. Not engaged to sing there but as a client the same as we were. Eventually someone asked Billie to sing and she did not refuse. I've always dug Lady Day from the first time I heard her, so this pleased me to hear her once again in person. And it was a great thrill for Lily because she liked her records very much and now she could see and hear the Lady Day in the flesh.

Oscar would not let me pay for anything and somewhere during the morning, we had picked up Al Hall who was with us at Minton's. We left Teddy Hill about 6 a.m. and Al suggested that we go to his place for breakfast. We also had with us Joan Hill, who had been my common law step-daughter, if some law of that kind exists. Joan didn't get along too well with her mother, Beezie. She was twenty years old, six feet tall and had a baby of six months, Steve. She left us to go and fetch the baby and said she would rejoin…

Al was living on 52nd street not far from the pier, which I think was at 42nd street and Riverside Drive. Lily and I were in a hotel at 25th street and 7th Avenue. We had packed our baggage and had to go and get them with a taxi.
